name: Amazon SES
summary: Amazon Simple Email Service sends through an API or an SMTP interface and charges $0.10 per 1,000 outbound emails pay as you go. Bounce and complaint data arrives through notifications or event publishing, and you build your own log views from that data.

facts.text: SES documents three ways to send: the console for tests, the SMTP interface, and the API.
Event publishing reports sends, deliveries, opens, clicks, bounces, complaints and rejects with details on each event, through CloudWatch, Amazon Data Firehose or SNS, and extra charges apply.
Accounts started after November 25, 2019 use the account-level suppression list for bounces and complaints by default, and only hard bounces are added to it.
Gmail does not provide complaint data to SES, so a recipient who uses the Gmail Spam button is not added to the suppression list.

plans.name: Essentials
plans.unit: per 1,000 emails, first 10 million a month
plans.notes: No fixed fee listed. Falls to $0.14 above 10 million and $0.11 above 100 million

plans.name: Pro
plans.unit: per 1,000 emails, first 10 million a month
plans.notes: Fixed fee per account per region per month

plans.name: Enterprise
plans.unit: per 1,000 emails, first 10 million a month
plans.notes: Fixed fee per account per region per month

hiddenCosts: Standard dedicated IPs cost $24.95 a month per IP.
New AWS customers get up to $200 in credits. The free plan lasts 6 months, and credits must be used within 12 months of account creation.
Event publishing to CloudWatch carries separate charges.

contract.cancellation: The customer may end the agreement for any reason by notifying AWS and closing the account. Either side can end it for a material breach left uncured 30 days after notice. No minimum term is stated.
contract.dataExport: For 30 days after termination AWS does not remove customer content because of the termination, and it can be retrieved only if all amounts due are paid.
